one_sentence_story: When B. F. Skinner set a mechanical grain tray to open blindly every 15 seconds, six of eight hungry pigeons invented rigid personal dances because their reward circuits mistook coincidence for cause.
so_what_for_you: Whenever an unpredictable win lands right after a random habit — from lucky clothes to frantic button-mashing — pause and ask whether the timer would have paid out anyway.

jargon_map.plain: rewards delivered on a timer no matter what you do
jargon_map.analogy: like an automatic sprinkler turning on whether you dance for rain or stand still

jargon_map.plain: two events happening right next to each other in time
jargon_map.analogy: like clapping your hands the exact second thunder rumbles
like repeating a joke because the room laughed

jargon_map.plain: repeating a habit thousands of times after rewards stop
jargon_map.analogy: like clicking a dead TV remote twenty times

jargon_map.plain: restless pacing early in a wait versus focused pecking right before delivery
jargon_map.analogy: like pacing the kitchen while water heats, then hovering by the kettle at the whistle
